items: Water Entry into the Biotic Component: Water enters biotic components primarily through two methods. Terrestrial plants use root hairs to absorb water from the soil and use it for photosynthesis and as a structural support (turgor pressure). Animals take in water by drinking directly from freshwater sources and by eating food.

Water Exit from the Biotic Component: Once water has served its purpose inside an organism. it returns into the abiotic environment. Transpiration in plants is the major exit point for water. Plants release water vapors in atmosphere through the stomata present in their leaves. Respiration in plants and animals also produces water as a byproduct. This "metabolic water" is exhaled as vapors. In excretion and egestion, animals also release water through urine and feces, returning it to the soil or water bodies. During perspiration (sweating), animals release water through skin pores, which evaporates to the atmosphere. Decomposition of organisms’ dead bodies also releases water back into the soil or atmosphere.

blocks.alt: Two loops. Abiotic cycle (Loop 1, blue arrows): ocean, evaporation (sun), atmosphere, condensation, precipitation, surface runoff and infiltration into soil water, and back to the ocean. Biotic pathway (Loop 2, green arrows): soil water absorbed by plant roots into the plant body, transpiration to the atmosphere; plant body and precipitation to ingestion by animals and the animal body; respiration to the atmosphere, excretion to soil water.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 25.2 draws the 'Absorption by plant roots' arrow pointing back into the soil water and double-headed arrows between plant body, ingestion and animal body. Water moves one way, from soil water by absorption into the plant body and by ingestion into the animal body, as drawn above.
